clauses.statement: R1 is a planning-only contract preparation slice and is bound to the exact J0 source lock: Unson-LLC/brainbase PR #481, merge commit f8e7ac61349b326863feae5d7d3d8ae68e2b9d10, implementation head 3fd71a1da59a85cb7cdc8cce8b17f22e3b767bde.

The artifact identity is artifact_id=sha256:<64 lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of UTF-8(JCS(payload))>, where payload contains artifact schema version, exact J0 source lock, payload.run_id, and the complete JudgmentDAGRunRecord; the stored envelope separately contains artifact_id, envelope.run_id, and payload, and artifact_id, path, temporary name, time, and environment are excluded from the digest preimage.

Canonical serialization is RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS): it applies JCS property ordering, number serialization, Unicode/string escaping, UTF-8, and no whitespace; it preserves the semantic order of J0 arrays and rejects non-JSON values, cycles, sparse arrays, lone surrogates, unknown fields, wrong types, and incomplete values. JCS-nonconformant J0 records are rejected at save.

After pure JCS validation and digest calculation, save first acquires a per-run exclusive reservation; inside it, existing binding is checked, a conflicting loser is denied before temp creation, then a stored JCS(envelope) is written/fsynced to temp, atomically renamed and artifact-fsynced on the same filesystem, bound by create-once and binding-fsynced, then read back for commit verification. Reservation, temporary, artifact publish, binding publish, and commit verify I/O faults return storage_io_error with exact failure_phase and truthful effects; pre-existing committed bytes stay unchanged and incomplete states are never completed artifacts.

Given a first create-once run_id binding, when a save supplies different canonical content, artifact digest, source lock, schema version, or any mismatch among envelope.run_id, payload.run_id, and record.run_id, the store returns a run_id conflict and leaves the binding and existing artifact unchanged.

Given an artifact locator, when stored envelope bytes are tampered, truncated, zero-length, partially written, reordered, extended, bound to a different digest, or have envelope/payload/record run_id mismatch, reload recomputes the payload digest and envelope JCS bytes and rejects without returning a success record or repairing storage.

A successful reload returns a recursively deep-frozen snapshot detached from parser, storage, and caller references; mutation of the returned value cannot change saved bytes, identity, or a later reload.

Given an artifact_id, run_id, or locator containing traversal, absolute path, NUL, separator, dot segment, symlink, or non-regular file, or a cross-filesystem atomic claim, save and reload fail closed without root escape or symlink following. Fault injection at reservation/lock, temporary open/write/fsync and cleanup, rename/artifact fsync, binding create/fsync, and commit verify fixes storage_io_error, failure_phase, effects, and fresh-process readback; temporary and published-unbound states remain invisible until exact binding recovery or future maintenance cleanup.

Concurrent writers first serialize under a per-run exclusive reservation. Identical canonical content converges to one immutable artifact and is idempotent; different content for one run_id is denied before artifact publication for the loser and never uses last-write-wins.

A planned positive restart/reopen E2E saves a synthetic J0 record with store/process A, closes A, reopens the same root with fresh process/store B, reloads artifact_id, asserts exact original-record equality plus envelope/payload/record binding and J0 source-lock/schema equality, asserts recursive deep-freeze and mutation isolation, and records J0 runner invocation count as zero; no runtime or test is created in this planning slice.

Future RED tests must fail on pre-fix two-layer identity errors, RFC 8785 JCS key-order/number/Unicode/lone-surrogate fixture errors, envelope/payload/record run_id replacement, reservation-order violations, overwrite, tamper or truncation acceptance, symlink or traversal following, partial or published-unbound artifact visibility, concurrent last-write-wins, ambiguous cleanup, storage I/O failure collapsed to success/raw text/wrong phase or effects, and reload mutation.

This planning change modifies exactly six files: the Story, Architecture, draft Spec, Task, story-scoped VibePro draft, and existing .vibepro/config.json story registration; it creates no source-lock, schema, fixture, validator, source, test, runtime, database, Graph, customer, secret, or deployment artifact. current_story_id changes only unspecified VibePro defaults; a later disposable fixture must prove that an explicit J0 --story-id selects and writes only J0 while R1 review/artifact bytes and Git state remain unchanged.

Historical replay, runner version resolution, outcome attachment, evaluation event-set protection, baseline-candidate comparison, scoring, and calibration are deferred to later stories and are not implied by artifact save or reload.
